messages:
customer-ops: Customer acme-inc hitting intermittent 502s on Hosted API when using streaming responses. Started after a model swap around 2026-03-19 01:12 UTC. Client sees EOF then 502 from edge. sample request_id=req_8f3c2a, trace id trace-7b9c.

customer-ops: quick curl they ran: 
```
curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" --http2 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-open-xx
```

sasha: Is this eu1/frontdoor? any correlation id from our side?

customer-ops: eu1-frontdoor (hostedapi-eu1). They pasted the gateway response headers: 
```
HTTP/2 502
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_8f3c2a
server: envoy
```

raj: @maya-oncall can you grab envoy/nginx logs for req_8f3c2a and the upstream trace?

maya-oncall: pulling logs now. seeing these in envoy stderr around the time: 
```
[2026-03-19T01:12:21Z] envoy http2: RST_STREAM received, stream=45, error=PROTOCOL_ERROR
[2026-03-19T01:12:21Z] router: upstream reset: reset reason = connection termination
[2026-03-19T01:12:21Z] filter: unexpected trailer metadata: invalid-utf8 in header value
```

sasha: that "unexpected trailer metadata" line is interesting. Do we know if the model response emits trailers (e.g., for token-level metadata)?

tom: Customer client is a nodejs SSE consumer. They confirmed sending no trailers, but server-side (model agent) attaches a small trailer blob with debug-id which may be non-utf8 when compressed.

ingress-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026-112 created and linked to this thread.

devex: Can we reproduce locally? Suggest a focused curl that forces trailers: 
```
# simulate streaming + trailer (http2)
echo -e \":status: 200
content-type: text/event-stream

data: hello

--frame--



\" | nghttp -v -H \"te: trailers\" -d- https://localhost:8443/stream-test
```
```
# simpler: use our test harness to request model with streaming=true and attach a large metadata header on the model side
```
```
devex: Repro steps: spin test instance with model-agent env DEBUG_TRAILER_PAYLOAD=1 and issue same curl (http2 + -N). Observed envoy RST_STREAM and 502 at edge.
```

maya-oncall: root cause hypothesis: model-agent sometimes emits binary trailer metadata (non-utf8) which Envoy treats as malformed and resets the HTTP/2 stream leading to 502 from the gateway layer. This only happens when streaming chunks end with certain binary debug blobs.

sasha: Workaround for customer: set stream=false (non-streaming) or upgrade client to ignore trailers + retry on 502. Also we can flip a temporary proxy filter to drop trailers for hostedapi-eu1.

raj: Short-term mitigation: add an Envoy Lua filter to sanitize/discard trailer headers on frontdoor cluster. I'll prepare a small rollout to a canary pool.

maya-oncall: Adding guardrails: 1) watch for PROTOCOL_ERROR resets metric spike, 2) add alert when filter-drop-count > 10/min, 3) link to SUP ticket.

customer-ops: Customer applied stream=false and confirms errors stopped after 10m. They need streaming though. They asked ETA for permanent fix.

devex: Long-term: patch model-agent to base64-encode trailer values or move debug metadata into initial payload (not trailers). We'll add a fast-fix on the hosted side to drop invalid trailers at the edge.

tom: I'll own the model-agent change (PR + test) — plan: validate trailer bytes as UTF-8 or base64 encode by default. Target PR by EOD + test in staging.

raj: I'll push the Envoy lua sanitizer to canary within next 2 hours and update this thread with rollout id.

maya-oncall: Canary rollout id=canary-2212 started. Monitoring for 30m.

ingress-bot: Canary completed with no impact, sanitizer dropped ~12 invalid trailers across canary nodes.

sasha: customer notified with mitigation and ETA for agent patch.

customer-ops: Customer replied: thanks, will test streaming again after patch.

maya-oncall: followups: add e2e regression test to ensure trailers don't contain raw binary; add alerting for unexpected trailer size >1KB.

tom: PR opened: github.com/redwood/model-agent/pull/483 — includes trailer validation + base64 fallback.

devex: closing note: marking support ticket resolved once customer confirms streaming works post-patch. Logged learnings in internal playbook under "edge-http2-trailers".

customer-ops: Confirmed after patch and edge sanitizer the customer's streaming resumed normally at 2026-03-19 05:30 UTC. No further 502s. Closing ticket. :white_check_mark:
